sentences.en: If you have teenagers or work closely with young people, chances are you've had mystifying conversations like this one.
sentences.zh: 如果你有青少年孩子或经常与年轻人打交道，你很可能会经历这种让人摸不着头脑的对话。

sentences.en: L.I.T.
sentences.zh: L.I.T.（超赞 / High爆）

sentences.en: It means that it's going to be exciting or fun and that you should be there.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是即将变得激动人心或有趣，而你应该去现场。

sentences.en: Like that party's going to be lit.
sentences.zh: 就像那个派对会非常火爆一样。

sentences.en: My producer Maggie Penman recently went on a slang-finding mission in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我的制作人玛吉·彭曼最近在华盛顿特区进行了一次寻找俚语的任务。

sentences.en: She ended up talking to a group of college students from American University.
sentences.zh: 她最后和美国大学的一群大学生交谈起来。

sentences.en: Yeah, turnt is another one.
sentences.zh: 对，“turnt”是另一个词。

sentences.en: But like, I don't know, what's turnt?
sentences.zh: 但比如说，我不知道，“turnt”究竟是什么？

sentences.en: It's one of those words that you just can't really define.
sentences.zh: 它是那种你真的无法下定义的词之一。

sentences.en: You just have to use it in the context.
sentences.zh: 你只能在语境中使用它。

sentences.en: Turnt.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It's going to be lit.
sentences.zh: 这会很火爆。

sentences.en: Turnt is used to describe lit.
sentences.zh: Turnt 是用来形容 lit 的。

sentences.en: So fun.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: It'll be lit at 11 p.m.
sentences.zh: 晚上11点时它会很火爆

sentences.en: and it'll be turnt at 1 a.m.
sentences.zh: 到了凌晨1点就会彻底 High 翻。

sentences.en: And then it'll be ratchet at 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 然后到了凌晨2点就会变得乱七八糟。

sentences.en: Ratchet?
sentences.zh: 乱七八糟？

sentences.en: Yeah, ratchet's like, oh my gosh, everybody's sloppy.
sentences.zh: 对，ratchet 就像是，哦天哪，所有人都散漫得一塌糊涂。

sentences.en: This isn't fun anymore.
sentences.zh: 这已经一点都不好玩了。

sentences.en: This is just ratchet.
sentences.zh: 这简直太下头了。

sentences.en: Young people have always used language in new and different ways.
sentences.zh: 年轻人总是以新颖独特的方式使用语言。

sentences.en: And it has pretty much always driven older people crazy.
sentences.zh: 而且这几乎总是把老年人气得够呛。

sentences.en: On fleek is usually used in relation to somebody's eyebrows.
sentences.zh: On fleek 通常用来形容某人的眉毛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because eyebrows are a big trend right now.
sentences.zh: 因为现在眉毛是一个巨大的潮流。

sentences.en: If you have great eyebrows, you're like pretty.
sentences.zh: 如果你有极好的眉毛，你就显得很漂亮。

sentences.en: So that's like the new thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这是现在流行的新做法。

sentences.en: And usually, it came from Instagram.
sentences.zh: 而且通常它源自 Instagram。

sentences.en: Whenever somebody, like I just saw it like five minutes ago on somebody's Instagram,
sentences.zh: 每当有人——就像我五分钟前在某人的 Instagram 上看到的那样——

sentences.en: they had great eyebrows.
sentences.zh: 他们的眉毛画得极好。

sentences.en: They obviously just penciled them in.
sentences.zh: 他们显然刚用眉笔勾勒过。

sentences.en: And all the comments were like, OMG, those eyebrows are on fleek.
sentences.zh: 所有的评论都在说，天哪，这眉毛简直完美至极。

sentences.en: Extra E's.
sentences.zh: 加长版的 E。

sentences.en: Oh, like 12 E's, at leaSt. The more the E's, the better.
sentences.zh: 哦，比如至少有12个 E。E 越多越好。

sentences.en: All those likes and literallys and extra E's might sometimes grate on your nerves.
sentences.zh: 所有这些“like”、“literally”和拉长的 E 有时可能会让你感到烦躁。

sentences.en: But my guest, John McWhorter, says the problem might be with you, not them.
sentences.zh: 但我的嘉宾约翰·麦克沃特说，问题可能出在你身上，而不是他们。

sentences.en: Language is a parade.
sentences.zh: 语言是一场游行。

sentences.en: And nobody sits at a parade wishing that everybody would stand still.
sentences.zh: 没有人会坐在游行队伍里希望所有人都站着别动。

sentences.en: John McWhorter is a professor of English and comparative literature at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦克沃特是哥伦比亚大学的英语和比较文学教授。

sentences.en: He's also the author of a new book, Words on the Move.
sentences.zh: 他也是一本新书《语言在流变》的作者。

sentences.en: Why English won't and can't sit still, like literally.
sentences.zh: 为什么英语过去不会、现在也不会、将来也永远不可能一成不变，就拿 literally 来说。

sentences.en: So this is, like literally, Hidden Brain, and I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 所以这里是——可以说字面意义上的——《隐藏的大脑》，我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This week's episode is going to be lit, it's going to be turnt, and it's going to be on fleek.
sentences.zh: 本周的节目将会非常火爆，将会彻底 High 翻，而且会完美至极。

sentences.en: We hope it's not going to be ratchet.
sentences.zh: 我们希望它不会变得乱七八糟。

sentences.en: John McWhorter, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦克沃特，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Many of us have dictionaries at home or at work, John.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我们很多人在家里或工作时都有字典。

sentences.en: And you say that dictionaries, in some ways, paint an unrealistic portrait of a language.
sentences.zh: 而你说字典在某种程度上描绘了一幅不切实际的语言画像。

sentences.en: They give us a sense that the meanings of words are fixed, when in fact they're not.
sentences.zh: 它们给我们一种印象，认为词义是固定不变的，而事实上并非如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, dictionaries are wonderful things, but they create an illusion that there's such thing as a language that stands still.
sentences.zh: 是的，字典是极好的东西，但它们制造了一种错觉，让人觉得存在一种一成不变的语言。

sentences.en: When really, it's the nature of human language to change.
sentences.zh: 然而实际上，人类语言的本质就是不断变化。

sentences.en: Each generation hears things and interprets things slightly differently from the previous one.
sentences.zh: 每一代人听到的事物和对事物的理解都与前一代人略有不同。

sentences.en: And I mean just in terms of even sounds changing, in the way that you put words together, changing bit by bit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅就发音的变化、组合词语的方式而言，都在一点一点地改变。

sentences.en: And there's never been a language that didn't do that.
sentences.zh: 从来没有哪种语言不曾经历过这种变化。

sentences.en: I love this analogy you have in the book, where you mention how, you know, thinking that a word has only one meaning
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢你在书中的那个比方，你提到，你知道，认为一个词只有一个含义

sentences.en: is like looking at a snapshot taken at one point in a person's life and saying,
sentences.zh: 就像看着一个人在生命某个时间点拍摄的快照然后说：

sentences.en: this photograph represents the entirety of what this person looks like.
sentences.zh: 这张照片代表了这个人生存的全貌。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: It's as if you saw a person, I'm not going to say at four, because then the person is growing up.
sentences.zh: 这就好像你看到一个人，我不会说四岁时，因为那时人还在成长。

sentences.en: And if I use that analogy, then it seems like I'm saying that language grows up or it moves towards something or it develops.
sentences.zh: 如果我用那个比喻，就会显得我好像在说语言在长大，或者它在朝某个方向前进，或者在发展。

sentences.en: Imagine you meet somebody, they're 39, and you take their picture.
sentences.zh: 想象你遇到一个人，他们39岁，你给他们拍了一张照片。

sentences.en: And then 10 years later, when they're 49, you say, well, that picture of you at 39 is what you really are.
sentences.zh: 然后在10年后，当他们49岁时，你说，嗯，你39岁时的那张照片才是真正的你。

sentences.en: And whatever has happened to you since then is some sort of disaster, something that shouldn't have happened.
sentences.zh: 而此后发生在你身上的任何事都是某种灾难，是本不该发生的事。

sentences.en: How come you aren't exactly the way you were 10 years ago?
sentences.zh: 你怎么不像10年前那样一模一样了呢？

sentences.en: That's the way words are, too.
sentences.zh: 词语也是这样的。

sentences.en: But it's so hard to feel that, partly because our brains are on writing, as I say in the book.
sentences.zh: 但要感受到这一点非常困难，部分原因正如我在书中说的，我们的大脑被文字占据了。

sentences.en: We can't help, as literate people,
sentences.zh: 作为识字的人，我们禁不住

sentences.en: thinking that the real language is something that sits still with letters written all nice and pretty on a page that can exist for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 认为真正的语言是某种一动不动的东西，字母被精美漂亮地写在纸上，可以存在几百年。

sentences.en: But that's not what language has ever been.
sentences.zh: 但语言从来都不是那样的。

sentences.en: Only a couple hundred languages, or if you want to be conservative about it, a hundred languages are written in any real way.
sentences.zh: 只有区区几百种语言，或者保守一点说，一百种语言以真正的方式被文字化。

sentences.en: And then there's 6,800 others.
sentences.zh: 然后还有其他6800种语言。

sentences.en: Language is something that's spoken, and spoken language especially always keeps changing.
sentences.zh: 语言是用来口头表达的东西，尤其是口头语言，总是在不断变化。

sentences.en: It's inherent.
sentences.zh: 这是它固有的属性。

sentences.en: One of the points you make in the book, of course, is that the evolution of words and their meanings is what gives us this flowering of hundreds or thousands of languages.
sentences.zh: 你在书中提出的观点之一，当然是词语及其含义的演变赋予了我们成百上千种语言的繁荣。

sentences.en: Mistakes and errors are what turned Latin into French.
sentences.zh: 失误和错误正是将拉丁语变成法语的原因。

sentences.en: Yes, that's exactly true.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: What we think of today as a word undergoing some odd development or people using some new construction is exactly how Latin turned into French.
sentences.zh: 我们今天认为正在经历某种奇怪演变的词，或者人们使用某种新结构的方式，正是拉丁语变成法语的途径。

sentences.en: It's exactly how Old English turned into Modern English.
sentences.zh: 这也是古英语变成现代英语的方式。

sentences.en: And I don't think any of us are thinking that it's a shame that we're not using the language of Beowulf.
sentences.zh: 我想我们当中没有人会觉得没能使用《贝奥武夫》的语言是一种遗憾。

sentences.en: So I think that nobody would say that they don't think language should change.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为没有人会说他们认为语言不应该改变。

sentences.en: But what most people mean is that there'll be slang, that there'll be new words for new things, and that some of those words will probably come from other languages.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人的意思是，会有俚语，会有新事物的新词，其中一些词可能来自其他语言。

sentences.en: But I don't think that it's always clear to us that language has to change in that things are going to come in that we're going to hear as intrusions or as irritating or as mistakes,
sentences.zh: 但我不认为我们总是清楚地意识到语言必须发生变化，新事物会涌入，我们会将其视为侵扰、烦恼或错误，

sentences.en: despite the fact that that's how you get from, say, Old Persian to Modern Persian.
sentences.zh: 尽管事实正是通过这种方式，你才能从比如古波斯语演变为现代波斯语。

sentences.en: And nobody wishes that we hadn't developed our modern languages today from the ancient versions.
sentences.zh: 没有人希望我们今天的现代语言没有从古代版本演变而来。

sentences.en: I want to talk in the second half of our conversation about why the meanings of words change.
sentences.zh: 在我们的第二部分对话中，我想讨论词义为什么会改变。

sentences.en: But I want to start by talking about how they change.
sentences.zh: 但我首先想讨论它们是如何改变的。

sentences.en: Let's start with the word literally.
sentences.zh: 让我们从 literally 这个词开始。

sentences.en: It turns out, as you point out, that in common usage, literally literally means the opposite of literally.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，正如你所指出的，在日常用法中，literally 的字面意思恰恰与 literally 相反。

sentences.en: The second button literally makes or breaks the shirt.
sentences.zh: 第二颗纽扣简直直接决定了这件衬衫的成败。

sentences.en: Look at it.
sentences.zh: 你看它。

sentences.en: It's too high.
sentences.zh: 它太高了。

sentences.en: Dr. Harris, you are literally the meanest person I've ever met.
sentences.zh: 哈里斯博士，你简直是我见过的最刻薄的人。

sentences.en: In the first days, literally the first days.
sentences.zh: 在最初的日子里，真的就是最初的日子。

sentences.en: Literally stood.
sentences.zh: 字面意思稳稳站住了。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: We're literally making.
sentences.zh: 我们简直是在打造。

sentences.en: We're literally on the verge.
sentences.zh: 我们简直就在边缘。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it irritates people.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很惹人恼火。

sentences.en: But there's a different way of seeing literally.
sentences.zh: 但看待 literally 还有另一种方式。

sentences.en: If you take literally in what we can think of as its earliest meaning,
sentences.zh: 如果你把 literally 视为我们可以理解的它的最早含义，

sentences.en: the earliest meaning known to us is by the letter.
sentences.zh: 我们所知的最早含义是“逐字地”。

sentences.en: And so somebody says something literally.
sentences.zh: 因此有人字面意思地说某事。

sentences.en: Somebody takes a point literally.
sentences.zh: 有人字面理解某个观点。

sentences.en: Well, if you have a word like that, and if it's an intensifier of that kind,
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你有一个这样的词，如果它是一种那样的加强语气词，

sentences.en: you can almost guess that literally is going to come to mean something more like just really.
sentences.zh: 你几乎可以猜到 literally 最终会变得更像是“真的”或“简直”。

sentences.en: So what happens is that once literally comes to feel like it means really,
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，一旦 literally 感觉像是“真的”的意思，

sentences.en: people start using it in figurative constructions such as I was literally dying of thirSt.
sentences.zh: 人们就开始在比喻结构中使用它，例如我当时简直快渴死了。

sentences.en: Now, many people hear that and they think, well, that's no good because now literally can mean its opposite.
sentences.zh: 现在，许多人听到这个会想，嗯，这不好，因为现在 literally 可以表示它的反义词了。

sentences.en: But we have plenty of words like that in English where it doesn't bother us at all.
sentences.zh: 但在英语中我们有很多这样的词，它们一点也不让我们感到困扰。

sentences.en: For example, if you take seeds and put them in the ground, that's one thing.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你拿种子把它们种在地里，那是一回事。

sentences.en: But if you seed a watermelon, nobody assumes that you're taking seeds and putting them in the watermelon.
sentences.zh: 但如果你给西瓜去籽（seed a watermelon），没有人会假设你是把种子放进西瓜里。

sentences.en: You're taking them out.
sentences.zh: 你是把它们拿出来。

sentences.en: Those are called contronyms and literally has become a new contronym.
sentences.zh: 这些被称为兼类反义词，而 literally 已经成为一个新的兼类反义词。

sentences.en: It should be thought of as fun.
sentences.zh: 它应该被认为是有趣的。

sentences.en: So you make the case that the meanings of words change all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以你提出这样一个观点：词义一直在改变。

sentences.en: It's a bold argument that we should in some ways welcome it when people do their own thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大胆的论点，即在某种程度上，当人们特立独行时，我们应该欢迎它。

sentences.en: But I have to say, I noticed that you had a book out a few years ago that seemed to say the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，我注意到你几年前出过一本书，似乎在表达相反的观点。

sentences.en: And it was titled Doing Our Own Thing, The Degradation of Language and Music, and Why We Should Like Care.
sentences.zh: 它的书名是《做我们自己：语言和音乐的退化，以及我们为什么应该像在乎一下一样在乎》。

sentences.en: Does the new John McWhorter have a disagreement with the old John McWhorter?
sentences.zh: 现在的约翰·麦克沃特是在和过去的约翰·麦克沃特唱反调吗？

sentences.en: That's a very rich question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常深刻的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's getting to the point where I've been in the business a while and there are decisions I made back in my rollicking 30s, which I wouldn't make now.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，情况已经到了我在这个行业待了一段时间的地步，我在放荡不羁的30多岁时做出了一些决定，换作现在我是不会做的。

sentences.en: And Doing Our Own Thing was one where I allowed a subtitle that I shouldn't have because the publishers thought that that would make it sell better.
sentences.zh: 《做我们自己》就是其中之一，我允许使用了一个本不该采用的副标题，因为出版商认为这能让书卖得更好。

sentences.en: And I think it did.
sentences.zh: 我想确实如此。

sentences.en: But that book wasn't really about the degradation of language and music.
sentences.zh: 但那本书其实并不是关于语言和音乐的退化。

sentences.en: To this day, I hear sometimes that I've written somewhere that rap is terrible music and that it makes people pull their pants down and kill each other.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，我有时还是会听到有人说我曾在某处写过说唱是糟糕的音乐，它让人脱下裤子并自相残杀。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of it is because of just the music in that subtitle, when actually I didn't say anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我想很大程度上是因为那个副标题里的“音乐”一词，而实际上我根本没说过那样的话。

sentences.en: Actually, a lot of people really hated that book.
sentences.zh: 事实上，很多人真的很讨厌那本书。

sentences.en: That book disappointed a lot of people who thought they were going to get something like Lintruss's Eat, Shoots, and Leaves.
sentences.zh: 那本书让许多以为能读到类似林特拉斯的《吃、射与留》之类作品的人大失所望。

sentences.en: I never wrote such a book.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有写过这样的书。

sentences.en: And there are people mad at me to this day for tricking them by allowing that subtitle.
sentences.zh: 直到今天还有人对我很生气，因为我允许使用那个副标题把他们给“骗”了。

sentences.en: One of the things I found really interesting is that the evolution of words and language is constant.
sentences.zh: 我发现非常有趣的一点是，词语和语言的演变是持续不断的。

sentences.en: So new words are as likely to evolve as old ones.
sentences.zh: 因此，新词和旧词演变的几率是一样的。

sentences.en: And so LOL was an internet abbreviation meaning laugh out loud or laughing out loud.
sentences.zh: 所以 LOL 是一个互联网缩写，意思是哈哈大笑（laugh out loud 或 laughing out loud）。

sentences.en: But LOL in common usage today doesn't necessarily mean hysterical laughter.
sentences.zh: 但 LOL 在今天的日常用法中并不一定意味着歇斯底里的狂笑。

sentences.en: No, because LOL was an expression.
sentences.zh: 不，因为 LOL 是一种表达方式。

sentences.en: It was a piece of language.
sentences.zh: 它是一段语言。

sentences.en: And so you knew that its meaning was going to change.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道它的含义将会改变。

sentences.en: The only question was in which way.
sentences.zh: 唯一的疑问是以何种方式改变。

sentences.en: And it ended up becoming less a direct reflection of hearty laughter than an indication of the kind of almost subconscious laughter that we do in any kind of conversation that's meant as friendly.
sentences.zh: 它最终变得与其说直接反映开怀大笑，不如说更像是我们在任何旨在友好的对话中所表现出的那种几乎是潜意识的笑声的指示词。

sentences.en: It can be almost counterintuitive to listen to how much giggling and laughing you do in ordinary, actually rather plain exchanges with people.
sentences.zh: 听听你在普通、甚至相当平淡的交流中发出多少咯咯笑和笑声，有时可能会显得反直觉。

sentences.en: It's part of a general running indication that everything's okay between you and the other person, just like one's expected to smile a little bit in most interactions.
sentences.zh: 它是全面持续表明你和对方之间一切正常的表现之一，就像人们被期望在大多数互动中微微一笑一样。

sentences.en: So LOL starts out as meaning hearty, har, har, but then it becomes something more abstract.
sentences.zh: 所以 LOL 最初的意思是爽朗的大笑，但随后它变得更加抽象。

sentences.en: But the reason that it seems so elusive is because we don't really think about the quote-unquote meaning of things like our conversation easing laughter.
sentences.zh: 但它之所以显得如此难以捉摸，是因为我们并不真正去思考诸如“缓解谈话气氛的笑声”这种所谓的含义。

sentences.en: We actually also heard this idea from the students Maggie talked to in Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上也从玛吉在华盛顿交谈的学生那里听到了这个想法。

sentences.en: We make fun of people who use LOL in text messages, but I see that I'm using it more than ever, but more in a sassy way.
sentences.zh: 我们取笑那些在短信中使用 LOL 的人，但我发现我比以往任何时候都更多地使用它，但更多是出于一种俏皮的语气。

sentences.en: So if my roommate were to say something along the lines of, can I have the room from 10 to 12 and I'm trying to take a nap, I'll be like, LOL, no.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我的室友说出诸如“我10点到12点能用一下房间吗我要小睡一会儿”之类的话，我会说：LOL，不行。

sentences.en: So just to kind of ease it, like ease the hit of the rejection.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是为了缓和一下气氛，就像冲淡拒绝带来的打击一样。

sentences.en: As someone who spends a lot of his time listening to language evolve, John hears a lot of slang.
sentences.zh: 作为长期研究语言演变的人，约翰听过很多俚语。

sentences.en: He's a defender of language on the move, but I wanted to know if there were things that irritated even him.
sentences.zh: 他是行进中语言的捍卫者，但我很想知道是否有些事连他也会感到恼火。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, I'm a human being.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，我是个凡人。

sentences.en: And so even though I insist that there is no scientific basis for rejecting some new word or some new meaning or some new construction,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管我坚信排斥某些新词、新含义或新结构是没有科学依据的，

sentences.en: I certainly have my visceral biases.
sentences.zh: 但我确实有我内心的偏见。

sentences.en: And so, for example, can I get a hamburger?
sentences.zh: 比如，能给我来个汉堡吗？

sentences.en: Can I get some chicken?
sentences.zh: 能给我来点鸡肉吗？

sentences.en: I've always found that a very grating way to ask for something at a store.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得在店里这样点东西非常刺耳。

sentences.en: It seems kind of elliptical.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点省略过头了。

sentences.en: Like, would it be possible that I obtained?
sentences.zh: 就像是，我获得某物这种事可能发生吗？

sentences.en: And then if you are going to be that elliptical, why use the casual word get?
sentences.zh: 既然你要省略成这样，为什么还要用“get”这个随意的词？

sentences.en: And it sounds a little bit abrupt and grabby, like you're going to get something instead of being given.
sentences.zh: 而且这听起来有点唐突和生硬，好像你要去夺取某物，而不是被给予某物。

sentences.en: All of these are very subjective things.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是非常主观的事情。

sentences.en: It's not necessarily may I please have, but may I have, I'll have, but not can I get a.
sentences.zh: 这不一定非得是“请问我能要”，而是“我能要”、“我要”，但绝不是“我能拿个”。

sentences.en: I find it just vulgar for reasons that, as you can see, I can't even do what I would call defending.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这纯粹很粗俗，原因如你所见，我甚至无法做出我所谓的辩护。

sentences.en: It's just how I feel.
sentences.zh: 这只是我的感觉。

sentences.en: You're going to have feelings like that.
sentences.zh: 你总会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: And when I listen to people having their P's, I don't think, stop it.
sentences.zh: 当我听到人们说那些让人挑剔的话时，我不会想：住手。

sentences.en: But what I am thinking is you should realize that even if you don't like it, there's nothing wrong with it in the long run.
sentences.zh: 但我在想的是，你应该意识到，即使你不喜欢它，从长远来看它也没有任何问题。

sentences.en: Because, for example, Jonathan Swift didn't like it that people were saying kissed instead of kissed and rebuked instead of rebuked.
sentences.zh: 因为，举个例子，乔纳森·斯威夫特就不喜欢人们把“kissed”说成别的音，或者把“rebuked”说成别的音。

sentences.en: He didn't like that people were shortening the words.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢人们缩短单词。

sentences.en: How does that sound now?
sentences.zh: 现在听起来怎么样？

sentences.en: We don't want to be like that.
sentences.zh: 我们不想变成那样。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think it might be time for me to confess one of my pet peeves.
sentences.zh: 我想也许是我该坦白我的一大宠物恨（最讨厌的事）的时候了。

sentences.en: It has to do with the word momentarily.
sentences.zh: 这和“momentarily”这个词有关。

sentences.en: Growing up, I understood this word to mean for a very short time, as in John McWhorter was momentarily surprised.
sentences.zh: 在我成长过程中，我理解这个词的意思是“非常短暂的一小会儿”，比如“约翰·麦克沃特短暂地惊讶了一下”。

sentences.en: But I find that people now usually use the word to mean very soon, as in we're going to board the plane momentarily.
sentences.zh: 但我发现人们现在通常用这个词来表示“很快”，比如“我们马上就要登机了”。

sentences.en: The dictionary says both uses are correct.
sentences.zh: 字典上说这两种用法都是正确的。

sentences.en: But, you know, John, something gnaws at me every time I hear the word used wrong.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，约翰，每次听到这个词被错误使用，我心里总有点不是滋味。

sentences.en: And after listening to you, I realize I might have to finally give in.
sentences.zh: 听了你的话后，我意识到我可能最终不得不妥协了。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask you about why languages change and whether there are hidden rules that shape why some words are more likely to evolve than others.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我将问你为什么语言会发生变化，以及是否存在隐形规则来决定为什么有些词比其他词更有可能演变。

sentences.en: We'll be back momentarily.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿就回来。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: John, you've noted that humans have been using language for tens of thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 约翰，你曾指出人类使用语言已有几万年历史了。

sentences.en: But for most of that time, language was talking.
sentences.zh: 但在绝大部分时间里，语言就是说话。

sentences.en: Writing came along relatively recently.
sentences.zh: 书面语出现的时间相对较晚。

sentences.en: Are the spoken origins of language one reason that words are so often on the move?
sentences.zh: 语言的口头起源是词汇经常在变动的原因之一吗？

sentences.en: Yes, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 是的，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: That's exactly it.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Language, as it evolved, was just talking to an extent that can be very hard for we literate people to imagine.
sentences.zh: 语言在演变的过程中，很大程度上就是纯粹的说话，这种程度是我们这些识字的人很难想象的。

sentences.en: There was no way of transcribing an approximation of what people said, and nobody would have thought of doing it.
sentences.zh: 当时没有什么方法可以把人们说的话近似地记录下来，而且也没有人会想到去做这件事。

sentences.en: Language was talk.
sentences.zh: 语言就是交谈。

sentences.en: When language was like that, of course, it changed a lot, fast, because once you said it, it was gone.
sentences.zh: 当语言是这样的时候，它当然会快速地发生很大变化，因为一旦你说出口，它就消失了。

sentences.en: And if people heard the sounds a little differently and produced them a little differently, if there were new meanings of words, very quickly,
sentences.zh: 如果人们对声音的听感略有不同，发音也略有不同，如果词汇有了新的含义，很快地，

sentences.en: whatever the original meaning was wouldn't be remembered.
sentences.zh: 最初的意思就不会被记住了。

sentences.en: There was no such thing as looking up what it originally meant.
sentences.zh: 根本没有什么去查证它最初意思这回事。

sentences.en: And so language changed, just like the clouds and the sky.
sentences.zh: 所以语言就像云彩和天空一样不断变化。

sentences.en: But then you start writing things down, and you're in a whole new land, because once things are sitting there written on that piece of paper, there's that illusion.
sentences.zh: 但后来你开始把事情写下来，你就进入了一片全新大陆，因为一旦事情静静地写在那张纸上，就会产生一种错觉。

sentences.en: And it really is an illusion that what language is is something that sits still.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种错觉，以为语言是一种静止不动的东西。

sentences.en: There's a way of speaking right, and the way you speak right is not by speaking the way the people around you in your life speak,
sentences.zh: 有一种所谓的正确说话方式，而正确说话的方式不是像你生活中周围的人那样说话，

sentences.en: but by speaking the way the language is as it sits there all nice and pretty on that piece of paper where its reality exists.
sentences.zh: 而是按照语言静静地、漂漂亮亮地存在于那张纸上的现实去说话。

sentences.en: Would it be possible to use what we have learned about how words and languages evolve to potentially write what a dictionary might look like in 50 years or 100 years?
sentences.zh: 我们是否可以利用我们对词汇和语言如何演变的了解，来预测字典在50年或100年后可能会是什么样子？

sentences.en: You could have fun doing such a thing.
sentences.zh: 做这种事会很有趣。

sentences.en: The fact is that language change can always go in one of many directions.
sentences.zh: 事实是，语言的变化总是可以朝多个方向发展中的一个发展。

sentences.en: There's a chance element to it.
sentences.zh: 其中包含偶然的因素。

sentences.en: So you can't know how the words are going to come out, but you can take good guesses.
sentences.zh: 所以你无法确切知道词汇将如何演变，但你可以做出很好的猜测。

sentences.en: You know, endings are going to tend to drop off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，词尾往往会脱落。

sentences.en: So if you took a bunch of those tendencies, you could make up, say, the English of 50 years from now.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你采纳一堆这样的趋势，你可以杜撰出比如说50年后的英语。

sentences.en: But some of the things would just be complete chance.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情完全是纯粹的巧合。

sentences.en: You would never know, for example, that...
sentences.zh: 比如说，你永远不会知道……

sentences.en: I'll give you an example I've actually been thinking about.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个我其实一直在思考的例子。

sentences.en: Women under about 30 in the United States, when they're excited or they're trying to underline a point, putting a at the end of things.
sentences.zh: 美国30岁以下的女性，当她们感到兴奋或试图强调某个观点时，会在句尾加上一个“a”。

sentences.en: And so somebody will say, well, who was it who you thought was going to give you this present?
sentences.zh: 所以有人会说，嗯，你以为是谁要送你这份礼物？

sentences.en: You!
sentences.zh: 你！

sentences.en: And I mean, really, it sounds exactly like that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的，听起来完全就是这样。

sentences.en: I know!
sentences.zh: 我懂！

sentences.en: Is there.
sentences.zh: 就在那儿。

sentences.en: Or something along the lines of, babe!
sentences.zh: 或者类似的话，宝贝！

sentences.en: Babe!
sentences.zh: 宝贝！

sentences.en: And as odd as that sounds, I can guarantee you, if you watch any TV show with women under a certain age, or if you just go out on an American street and listen,
sentences.zh: 听起来可能很奇怪，但我向你保证，如果你看任何有特定年龄以下女性的电视剧，或者如果你只是走上美国街头去听听，

sentences.en: you'll find that that's a new kind of exclamatory particle.
sentences.zh: 你会发现这是一种新型的感叹词。

sentences.en: That is the most random thing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太随机了。

sentences.en: And I would really guess that in a few decades, men will be doing it, too.
sentences.zh: 我真的猜想，再过几十年，男性也会这么做。

sentences.en: Those sorts of things tend to start with women.
sentences.zh: 这类事情往往是从女性开始的。

sentences.en: You couldn't have predicted this.
sentences.zh: 你根本不可能预测到这一点。

sentences.en: I know!
sentences.zh: 我懂！

sentences.en: Move!
sentences.zh: 走开！

sentences.en: You can't know, but you can certainly know that if we could listen to people 50 years from now, they'd sound odd.
sentences.zh: 你无法确切知道，但你绝对可以确定，如果我们能听到50年后的人说话，他们听起来会很奇怪。

sentences.en: Something new will have started by then.
sentences.zh: 到那时一定会有新的东西出现。

sentences.en: Just like if we listened to people in 1971, they sound odd in that they don't say like as much as we do.
sentences.zh: 就像如果我们听1971年的人说话，他们听起来也很奇怪，因为他们不像我们这样频繁地使用“like”。

sentences.en: That hadn't started then.
sentences.zh: 那在当时还没开始呢。

sentences.en: Imagine how we would sound to them if they could hear us.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果他们能听到我们说话，我们在他们听来会是什么样。

sentences.en: Well, if you're so upset about it, maybe you can think of a way to help her.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你对这事这么心烦，也许你能想出一个帮她的办法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, lots of people blow off steam about something they think is wrong, but very few people are willing to get involved and do something about it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人对他们认为不对的事情大发牢骚，但很少有人愿意参与并为此做点什么。

sentences.en: I'm willing to get involved.
sentences.zh: 我愿意参与。

sentences.en: So all this raises a really interesting question.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切引发了一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: You know, we spend years teaching children about how to use language correctly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们花了好几年时间教导儿童如何正确使用语言。

sentences.en: As someone who works in media, I often find that people who can write well are often people who know how to think well.
sentences.zh: 作为一名媒体工作者，我经常发现擅长写作的人往往也是懂得如何思考的人。

sentences.en: So I often equate clarity of writing with clarity of thought.
sentences.zh: 所以我经常将文字的清晰等同于思维的清晰。

sentences.en: How do you balance the imperative of teaching correct usage, which I think is probably important, with the reality that this edifice that you're teaching is constantly crumbling?
sentences.zh: 你如何平衡教授正确用法的必要性（我认为这可能很重要）与你所教导的这座大厦正在不断坍塌的现实？

sentences.en: It's a matter of fashion, pure and simple.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是时尚问题，简单明了。

sentences.en: People do need to be taught what the socially acceptable forms are.
sentences.zh: 人们确实需要被教导什么是社会可接受的形式。

sentences.en: But what we should teach is not that the good way is logical and the way that you're comfortable doing it is illogical.
sentences.zh: 但我们应该教导的不是“好的方式是有逻辑的，而你习惯的方式是不合逻辑的”。

sentences.en: It should just be here is the natural way.
sentences.zh: 而应该只是“这是一种自然的方式”。

sentences.en: Then there's some things that you're supposed to do in public because that's the way it is, whether it's fair or not.
sentences.zh: 然后有些事情你本该在公众场合去做，因为事情就是这样，不管公平与否。

sentences.en: You can even teach people to have a little bit of fun with the artifice.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以教人们对这种人为造作的东西感到一点乐趣。

sentences.en: But it's exactly like it was maybe about 20 years ago that somebody, a girlfriend I had told me that if I wore pants that had little vertical pleats up near the waist,
sentences.zh: 但这完全就像大约20年前，我的一位女朋友告诉我，如果我穿腰部附近有细小垂直褶裥的裤子，

sentences.en: then I was conveying that I was kind of past it.
sentences.zh: 那么我就是在传达我已经过时的信息。

sentences.en: That was somehow a dad's fashion and that I should start wearing flat fronted pants.
sentences.zh: 不知为何那是老爸的时尚，我应该开始穿无褶前片的裤子。

sentences.en: That is utterly arbitrary that those little slits in American society look elderly.
sentences.zh: 在美国社会中，那些小褶缝看起来显得老气，这完全是随意的。

sentences.en: But for various chance reasons, that's what those slits came to mean.
sentences.zh: 但由于各种偶然的原因，那些褶缝就有了这种含义。

sentences.en: So I started wearing flat fronted pants.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始穿无褶前片的裤子。

sentences.en: That is exactly why you should say fewer books instead of less books in some situations.
sentences.zh: 这正是为什么在某些情况下你应该说“fewer books”而不是“less books”。

sentences.en: And yes, Billy and I went to the store rather than the perfectly natural Billy and me went to the store.
sentences.zh: 是的，是“Billy and I went to the store”，而不是完全自然的“Billy and me went to the store”。

sentences.en: Sometimes you just have to suck it up.
sentences.zh: 有时你只能逆来顺受。

sentences.en: But I think that we should learn not to listen to people using natural language as committing errors because there's no such thing as making a mistake in your language if a critical mass of other people speaking your language are doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们应该学会不要把使用自然语言的人视为在犯错，因为如果说你的语言的大多数核心人群都在这样做，那么在你的语言中根本就没有犯错这回事。

sentences.en: You make the case that concerns over the misuse of language might actually be one of the last places where people can publicly express prejudice and class differences.
sentences.zh: 你提出这样的观点：对误用语言的担忧实际上可能是人们公开表达偏见和阶层差异的最后阵地之一。

sentences.en: And as you point out, it's not just that people feel that a word is being misused.
sentences.zh: 正如你所指出的，不仅仅是人们觉得某个词被误用了。

sentences.en: They often feel angry about it.
sentences.zh: 他们往往为此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And you think this anger is actually telling.
sentences.zh: 而你认为这种愤怒其实说明了问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的这么认为。

sentences.en: I think that the tone that many people use when they're complaining that somebody says Billy and me went to the store is a little bit incommensurate with the significance of the issue.
sentences.zh: 我认为许多人在抱怨别人说“Billy and me went to the store”时所使用的语气，与这个问题的严重性有点不成比例。

sentences.en: And I can't help surmising that part of it is that the educated American has been taught, and often well, that you're not supposed to look down on people because of gender,
sentences.zh: 我不禁推测，部分原因是受过教育的美国人已经被灌输了一种观念（而且往往很深刻），即你不应该因为性别而看不起别人，

sentences.en: because of race, because of ability.
sentences.zh: 因为种族，因为能力。

sentences.en: But might we allow that there's probably a part of all human beings that wants to look down on somebody else?
sentences.zh: 但我们是否可以承认，所有人类内心深处可能都有一部分想要看不起别人？

sentences.en: What a cynical thing to say, but that doesn't mean that it might not be true.
sentences.zh: 说出这样的话真是愤世嫉俗，但这并不意味着它可能不是真的。

sentences.en: And if that is true,
sentences.zh: 如果那是真的，

sentences.en: then the educated person can look down on people who say Billy and me went to the store or who are using literally quote unquote wrong and condemn them in the kinds of terms that once were ordinary for condemning black people or women or what have you.
sentences.zh: 那么受过教育的人就可以看不起那些说“Billy and me went to the store”或者引用错误俗语的人，并用曾经用来谴责黑人、女性诸如此类的习以为常的言辞来谴责他们。

sentences.en: So I just think that it's something we need to check ourselves for.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是觉得这是我们需要反省自己的地方。

sentences.en: It might irritate you slightly to hear somebody say something like, I need less books instead of fewer books.
sentences.zh: 听到有人说出诸如“我需要less books而不是fewer books”之类的话，可能会让你稍微有点恼火。

sentences.en: But does a person who says that really deserve the kind of sneering condemnation that you often see?
sentences.zh: 但说这话的人真的配得上你经常看到的这种冷嘲热讽的谴责吗？

sentences.en: Something's off.
sentences.zh: 有些不对劲。

sentences.en: And I think it's because there's a lowlier part of our nature that grammar allows us to vent in the absence of other ways to do it that have not been available for some decades for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为语法让我们得以发泄人性中较低级的一部分，而在许多人看来，过去几十年里已经没有其他方式来做这件事了。

sentences.en: One of the ultimate messages I took from your work is that, you know, we can choose to have languages that are alive or languages that are dead and dead languages never change.
sentences.zh: 我从你的作品中得到的终极信息之一是，你知道，我们可以选择让语言充满活力或是让语言死去，而死去的语言永远不会改变。

sentences.en: And some of us might prefer those.
sentences.zh: 我们当中有些人可能更喜欢那些。

sentences.en: But if you prefer life, the unpredictability of life, then living languages in many ways are much more fun.
sentences.zh: 但如果你更喜欢生命、生命不可预测的活力，那么活的语言在许多方面要有趣得多。

sentences.en: Language is a parade and nobody sits at a parade wishing that everybody would stand still.
sentences.zh: 语言就像是一场游行，没有人会坐在游行队伍中希望所有人都站着别动。

sentences.en: If the language stayed the way it was, it would be like a pressed flower in a book.
sentences.zh: 如果语言保持原样，它就会像书本里夹着的一朵压扁的花。

sentences.en: Or as I say, I think it would be like some inflatable doll rather than a person.
sentences.zh: 或者正如我所说，我觉得它会像某种充气娃娃，而不是一个活生生的人。

sentences.en: I think that it's better to think of language as a parade that either you're watching or, frankly, that you're in, especially because the people are never going to stand still.
sentences.zh: 我认为最好把语言看作是一场游行，要么你在观看，要么坦白说，你就在其中，特别是人们永远不会停下脚步。

sentences.en: It's never happened.
sentences.zh: 这从未发生过。

sentences.en: It's never going to.
sentences.zh: 也绝不会发生。

sentences.en: And if you can enjoy it as a parade instead of wondering why people keep walking instead of just sitting on chairs and blowing on their tubas and not moving,
sentences.zh: 如果你能把它当作一场游行来欣赏，而不是纳闷为什么人们一直在走动，而不是坐在椅子上吹大号一动不动，

sentences.en: then you have more fun.
sentences.zh: 那么你就会收获更多乐趣。

sentences.en: I want everybody to have the fun I'm having.
sentences.zh: 我希望每个人都能体验到我正在享受的乐趣。

sentences.en: John McWhorter, thank you so much for joining me on Hidden Brain today.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦克沃特，非常感谢你今天做客《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: This episode of Hidden Brain was produced by Maggie Penman.
sentences.zh: 本期《隐藏的大脑》由玛吉·彭曼制作。

sentences.en: Our team includes Jenny Schmidt, Renee Klar, and our supervising producer, Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队包括珍妮·施密特、蕾妮·克拉尔，以及我们的监制塔拉·博伊尔。

sentences.en: This week, we also want to welcome two new people to our team, our new producer, Raina Cohen, and our spring intern, Chloe Connolly.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们还要欢迎两位新成员加入我们的团队，我们的新制作人雷娜·科恩，以及我们的春季实习生克洛伊·康诺利。

sentences.en: We're excited to have them on board.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴他们的加入。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero this week is Casey Herman.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的无名英雄是凯西·赫尔曼。

sentences.en: Casey is a producer on How I Built This and the TED Radio Hour.
sentences.zh: 凯西是《我是如何建立这个的》和《TED广播时间》的制作人。

sentences.en: In a former life, he worked in IT, which is something he never should have told his colleagues.
sentences.zh: 在过去的生活中，他从事过IT行业，这是他绝不应该告诉同事的事情。

sentences.en: We now bombard him with computer questions.
sentences.zh: 我们现在用各种电脑问题狂轰滥炸他。

sentences.en: Casey always has a friendly ear if you want to run an idea by someone smart.
sentences.zh: 如果你想找个聪明人商量一个想法，凯西随时都愿意倾听。

sentences.en: Casey, thanks for all the help.
sentences.zh: 凯西，谢谢你所有的帮助。

sentences.en: For more Hidden Brain, you can follow us on Facebook and Twitter and listen for my stories on your local public radio station.
sentences.zh: 想收听更多《隐藏的大脑》，你可以在脸书和推特上关注我们，并收听我在你当地公共广播电台播出的报道。

sentences.en: If you like this episode, please tell one friend who doesn't know about Hidden Brain about our show.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这一集，请向一位还不知道《隐藏的大脑》的朋友推荐我们的节目。

sentences.en: And tell us on social media whom you've tapped.
sentences.zh: 并在社交媒体上告诉我们你向谁推荐了。

sentences.en: We're always looking for new people to find the show.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在寻找新听众来发现我们的节目。

sentences.en: We have another request for you.
sentences.zh: 我们还有另一个请求。

sentences.en: Have you ever considered making a dramatic change in the way you consume the news?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾考虑过彻底改变你获取新闻的方式？

sentences.en: Many people say they've changed how and how much they listen to the news after the 2016 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 许多人表示，在2016年总统大选之后，他们改变了获取新闻的方式以及数量。

sentences.en: If you've ever made a big change in your news habits, we want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾对你的新闻收听习惯做出重大改变，我们希望听到你的声音。

sentences.en: Tell us what you've changed and how it's affected you.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们你改变了什么以及它如何影响了你。

sentences.en: We might feature your story in an upcoming episode that looks at whether there are healthy and unhealthy ways to consume the news.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会在即将播出的一期节目中采用你的故事，该节目将探讨是否存在健康和不健康的新闻获取方式。

sentences.en: Call and leave us a message at 661-772-7246.
That's 661-77-BRAIN.
sentences.zh: 也就是 661-77-BRAIN。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆，这里是NPR。

sentences.en: I'm in a sorority, so I hear everything.
sentences.zh: 我在一个女生联谊会里，所以我什么八卦都听得到。

sentences.en: This is a new up-and-coming one, so be ready.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新兴的、很有潜力的组织，所以做好准备。

sentences.en: LMK.
sentences.zh: 告诉我。

sentences.en: It's something people used to say in text.
sentences.zh: 这是人们以前在短信里常说的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, let me know.
sentences.zh: 对，就是“让我知道”。

sentences.en: But now everybody goes, is she really wearing that?
sentences.zh: 但现在每个人都在说，她真的穿成那样吗？

sentences.en: Let me know.
sentences.zh: 让我知道。

sentences.en: Or like LMK.
sentences.zh: 或者像 LMK 这样。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。
